purpose: Construct an explicit expanding flat-FLRW solution of the Einstein plus two-scalar equations whose growing kinetic gate remains inside a bounded positive-kinetic and positive-gradient domain of the committed dynamic-range theorem, retain any metric-cone violation, and bind an already-derived constant-kinetic split-gate architecture that escapes the theorem's hypotheses.

covariant_action.action: S=integral d^4x sqrt(-g)[M_Pl^2 R/2 + X + Z(u)Y]
covariant_action.invariants: X=-g^munu partial_mu(phi) partial_nu(phi)/2; Y=-g^munu partial_mu(chi) partial_nu(chi)/2; u=beta X^2
covariant_action.specialization: This witness sets the potentials, masses, ordinary matter, and direct matter metric couplings to zero. It is an exact member of the theorem's covariant action class, not a phenomenological force insertion.
covariant_action.scope: The metric and both scalar backgrounds are on shell. The exact high-frequency scalar kinetic/gradient block after Einstein lapse/shift constraints is mapped to the general P(X^IJ,phi^K) ADM result and is positive on the homogeneous trajectory, while the observed superluminal scalar eigenvalue is retained. No claim is made for causal metric-cone containment, the lower-order mass/mixing sector, late-time cosmology, radiative stability, or matter and photon phenomenology.

flrw_reduction.scalar_currents: J_phi=a^3 C sqrt(2X) and J_chi=a^3 Z sqrt(2Y), both constant
flrw_reduction.friedmann: 3 M_Pl^2 H^2=rho on the expanding branch
flrw_reduction.reconstruction: At each declared scale factor, eliminate Y=J_chi^2/[2 a^6 Z(X)^2] and solve the remaining J_phi equation only on 0<X<sqrt[1/(3 beta)]. On M>0 its derivative is [1+A M/Z^3]/sqrt(2X)>0 with A=J_chi^2/(2a^6)>0, proving at most one root in the healthy interval; the frozen upper-end sign check proves existence there before bisection.

principal_health.kinetic_matrix: K=[[1+Y(Z_X+2X Z_XX), 2 Z_X sqrt(XY)],[2 Z_X sqrt(XY),Z]]
principal_health.bounded_health_statement: For 0<u<1/3 and X,Y>0, Z,C,det(K) are strictly positive; the explicit trajectory additionally checks that both generalized scalar sound-speed-squared eigenvalues remain positive at every grid point. This is a ghost/gradient and constant-coefficient hyperbolicity statement, not a metric-cone causality statement.
principal_health.metric_cone_warning: The frozen witness has max(c_s^2)>1 and therefore does not establish that every scalar characteristic lies inside the g-null cone.
principal_health.einstein_constraint_mapping: For minimally coupled Einstein gravity plus P(X^IJ,phi^K), the constraint-reduced quadratic action has K_IJ=P_<IJ>+2 P_<MJ>,<IK> X^MK and spatial matrix P_<IJ>. Substitution of P=X+Z(X)Y gives exactly the frozen K and G, so lapse/shift constraints do not remove this high-frequency mixing or its superluminal eigenvalue.
principal_health.theorem_relation: The witness does not evade the dynamic-range theorem. It occupies a bounded positive-M interval and expands toward smaller u; extending the same gate through u=1/3 changes the sign of M.

general_multifield_perturbations.citation: Langlois, Renaux-Petel, Steer, and Tanaka, Phys. Rev. D 78, 063523 (2008)
general_multifield_perturbations.relation: Establishes the general P(X^IJ,phi^K) background equations and constraint-reduced quadratic scalar action used for the exact W21 mapping; it does not state the frozen q(u) dynamic-range corollary.

kinetic_screening_characteristics.citation: Bezares et al., Phys. Rev. D 104, 044022 (2021)
kinetic_screening_characteristics.relation: Demonstrates diverging scalar characteristic speeds in nonlinear k-essence collapse; it is neighboring breakdown evidence, not the two-scalar logarithmic-slope theorem.

screening_and_uv_constraints.relation: Constrains kinetic screening using resummation and positivity; it is a distinct UV-completion analysis and does not supply the frozen finite-range inequality.

field_dependent_kinetic_neighbors.citation: De Angelis and van de Bruck, JCAP 10 (2023) 023
field_dependent_kinetic_neighbors.relation: Studies a field-dependent two-field metric F(phi,chi), unlike the derivative-dependent normalization Z(X) analyzed here.

frozen_witness.units: dimensionless Planck units used only as an exact mathematical existence witness

escape_architecture.architecture: S_scalar=integral sqrt(-g)[P(X)-V(phi)+Y0 Y-m_chi^2 Z(X)chi^2/2] with constant Y0>0
escape_architecture.reason_it_escapes: The theorem's growing kinetic normalization is replaced by a constant chi kinetic coefficient, so Y_X=Y_XX=0 and the targeted second-order kinetic mixing combination is identically zero. The separately bound split-gate analysis retains its different amplitude and first-derivative risks.

publication_value.candidate_title: A finite dynamic-range obstruction for growing kinetic gates in two-scalar cosmology
publication_value.advance: The committed obstruction is supplemented by an explicit coupled Einstein-scalar on-shell witness on a bounded positive-kinetic/gradient interval, an explicit retained superluminal scalar warning, and a bound escape architecture, separating a finite-range design theorem from an unconditional no-go.
